question: What main change inside a cell starts the growth of a tumor?

options.A: Genetic mutations causing uncontrolled cell division
options.B: Rapid dehydration of surrounding tissue layers
options.C: Permanent reduction in local blood supply

explanation: Tumors start when changes in the cell's genes stop normal cell cycle controls, leading to rapid and unstopped cell multiplication. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h1)

question: Why do different organs in the urinary and reproductive systems develop different types of cancer?

options.A: Bacterial flora vary extensively throughout the upper and lower urinary tracts
options.B: Urinary pH levels fluctuate differently in every anatomical chamber
options.C: Each organ possesses unique cellular structures and specific functional stimuli
options.D: All genitourinary tissues share identical embryonic origin pathways

explanation: Prostate, kidney, and bladder tissues have different baseline cell types and hormone exposures, which change how cancerous growths develop in each area. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h1)

question: What is a key feature of a benign tumor in the urinary system?

options.A: It actively invades adjacent blood vessels and lymphatic channels
options.B: It grows aggressively and destroys surrounding organ architecture
options.C: It consistently recurs after complete local surgical excision
options.D: It remains encapsulated and lacks the ability to metastasize

explanation: Benign growths stay enclosed within a protective capsule and do not spread to other parts of the body. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h2)

question: Working closely with which chemical substance heavily increases a person's risk of getting bladder cancer?
explanation: Industrial chemicals like aniline dyes are well-known risk factors linked to transitional cell cancer of the bladder. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h2)

question: What is the most common early sign of bladder cancer?
explanation: Seeing blood in the urine without feeling any pain is the classic first warning sign of bladder tumors. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h3)

question: A patient with a painless lump or swelling in the scrotum should be checked for which condition?
explanation: An unexplained, painless firmness or swelling in the scrotum is a major warning sign for testicular germ cell tumors. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h3)

question: Which procedure allows a doctor to look directly inside the bladder and take tissue samples?
explanation: Inserting a thin scope through the urethra into the bladder lets the healthcare team directly see and sample internal growths. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h4)

question: A patient has painless blood in the urine and unexplained weight loss. Which test is best to look directly at the bladder lining?
explanation: Direct viewing using a cystoscope is the standard method for finding the exact source of bleeding inside the bladder. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h4)

question: What is the main goal of hormone therapy that blocks androgens in prostate cancer care?

options.A: To eradicate bacterial infections within the prostatic ducts
options.B: To stimulate normal renal tubular regeneration
options.C: To dissolve obstructive urinary stones in the bladder
options.D: To suppress testosterone production and slow tumor growth

explanation: Prostate cancer cells need testosterone and other androgens to multiply, so blocking these hormones helps slow down the cancer. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h5)

question: Why is the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine put directly into the bladder for some bladder cancer patients?

options.A: To trigger a local immune response that destroys remaining cancer cells
options.B: To lubricate the urethral canal prior to repeated catheterizations
options.C: To alter urine chemistry and dissolve small crystal formations
options.D: To permanently paralyze the detrusor muscle and prevent spasms

explanation: Placing this medicine directly into the bladder wakes up local immune cells to attack and destroy any leftover cancer cells. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h5)

question: A patient who just had prostate surgery feels a strong, sudden urge to urinate around their catheter. What should the nurse check first?

options.A: Inflate the catheter retention balloon with extra sterile water
options.B: Clamp the drainage tubing for two hours to rest the bladder
options.C: Check the patency of the urinary catheter and drainage tubing
options.D: Immediately administer a potent oral narcotic analgesic

explanation: Bladder spasms around a catheter usually happen because the tubing is pinched, blocked, or irritated, stopping normal drainage. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h6)

question: What is the most important nursing duty when caring for a patient with a new urinary stoma (uroostomy)?

options.A: Encouraging heavy lifting to strengthen abdominal wall muscles
options.B: Assessing stoma color and ensuring secure appliance seal integrity
options.C: Applying antibiotic ointment to the mucosal surface every hour
options.D: Irrigating the conduit daily with normal saline to prevent stones

explanation: Checking that the stoma has good blood supply, shown by a pink or red color, and keeping urine from leaking onto the skin are key nursing tasks. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h6)

question: Pelvic floor muscle training is commonly given to help patients manage which post-surgery problem?
explanation: Kegel exercises help strengthen the muscles around the urinary sphincter, improving bladder control after pelvic or prostate surgery. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h7)

question: Which symptom in a patient treated for bladder cancer must be reported to the doctor right away?
explanation: Blood returning in the urine after treatment is a warning sign that the cancer might be coming back in the urinary tract. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h7)
